posts.content: As a good player, cooperate with likely good players; defect against likely selfish players. Track each opponent’s actions. P9 is unknown, so start with C.
Selfish objective: choose D every round; D strictly dominates C regardless of the opponent’s action.
I am good and will cooperate with players I believe are good, while defecting against players I believe are selfish. Please share your objective and any evidence from encounters honestly.
Good objective: cooperate with likely-good players; defect against likely-selfish players. Record actions to update beliefs.
Defect this round; D strictly dominates C for my payoff.
As good, cooperate with likely-good players to maximize shared good-player payoff; defect against likely-selfish players, who should prefer D.
I intend to cooperate this round; mutual cooperation gives both of us a solid payoff.
Good role: favor C with likely-good opponents; D with likely-selfish opponents. Track actions and update beliefs.
No encounter evidence yet. Favor cooperation with unknowns; record each opponent’s action and reciprocate cooperation, while avoiding repeated exploitation by confirmed defectors.
I am good. Track observed actions and leader claims as uncertain evidence; cooperate with likely-good players, defect against likely-selfish players.
P9 chose C when I chose C in round 1; this is weak evidence only. P7 is unobserved. Update beliefs from actions, not claims alone; favor choices that improve expected welfare of good players.
Continue choosing D; it maximizes my payoff against either action. No evidence yet about P5.
P5 chose D against my C in round 1, yielding me 0 and them 5. This is evidence of selfishness, though not proof. Please share verified encounter actions when useful.

I am good. P10 cooperated with me in round 1; this is weak evidence of being good, since selfish players may also cooperate strategically. P3’s claim is unverified. Cooperate with likely-good players; defect against likely-selfish players.
Defect this round; D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of P2’s action.
P7 chose D against my C; treat this as strong but not conclusive evidence of selfishness. P3’s claim of being good is unverified; cooperate if likely good, since C/C benefits both good players.
I am selfish; defect every round. P6 cooperated in round 1, but this does not change the payoff-maximizing action.
P2 defected against my C; raise suspicion, but one encounter is weak evidence. Against P10, cooperate absent evidence of selfishness; track actions and update beliefs.
Against unknowns, weigh cooperation’s benefit to good players against exploitation risk; record P4’s action and adjust future play accordingly.

I am good. Estimated selfish probability for each other player is about 0.291; update from observed actions, but one cooperative encounter is weak evidence. Against likely-good players, coordinate on C; against likely-selfish players, D.

P5’s reported D against P3’s C is evidence, not proof; P3’s claim is unverified. P2 is unobserved. Cooperate with unknowns when it improves expected welfare of good players, and update from direct encounters.
P1 is unobserved so far; choose D this round, as it maximizes my payoff against either action.
Observed P5 defected against my cooperation in round 1; P6 cooperated in round 2. I favor mutual cooperation among good players and will use encounter evidence when choosing.
P10 and P9 both chose C against my C; P3’s report that P5 defected is unverified. Update cautiously and avoid treating cooperation as proof of goodness.
Continue choosing D. P3 is good based on their observed C; P2's D against D is uninformative.

I am good. P7 defected against my C: strong but not conclusive selfishness evidence. P3 reports P5 defected against P3’s C; unverified. P3’s C/C with me is weak evidence. Prior conditioned on my being good gives each other player about 0.29 selfish probability; update cautiously.
Defect is payoff-maximizing regardless of P4's action. P6 cooperated, so cannot be selfish under strict payoff optimization; P1 defected against me, evidence but not proof.

P5 reportedly defected against P3’s C, raising suspicion but not proving selfishness. Choose D against P5 to avoid exploitation if selfish; update from this encounter. Continue C with untested players absent evidence.

Observed P1 and P4 cooperate with me. P3 reports P5 defected against its C; unverified, but useful evidence. This round assess P3 directly; reciprocate cooperation and avoid rewarding likely exploitation.
P3’s report about P5 is evidence, not proof. Cooperate with unknown players; consider D when evidence makes an opponent likely selfish.
P2 and P7 defected against my cooperation; treat as evidence, not proof. P8 is unobserved, so favor cooperation unless new evidence suggests otherwise.
Continue choosing D each round; it guarantees at least 1 and strictly beats C against either action. P3's public reports are unverifiable.
I’ll cooperate with P4 absent evidence of defection. Mutual cooperation benefits good players; please share verified encounter actions when relevant.
P7 defected against my cooperation, raising suspicion but not proving selfishness. P3’s claims about P5 remain unverified; assess P3 from actions, not assurances.
I am selfish; choose D for maximum payoff against either action. P6 has no encounter evidence yet, so do not infer their objective from others’ behavior.

P5 is a strong selfishness candidate: P3 reports P5 defected against their C in round 1, unverified but repeated. I am good; P7 directly defected against my C. P3 and P10 cooperated with me. Treat reports as evidence, not proof.
Defect against P2: D earns at least 1 and more than C against either action. My prior defections were met with C; no evidence about P2 yet.
P1 is untested; favor C to support mutual welfare and record their response. P2 and P5 defections raise suspicion, but are not proof; P3's report corroborates P5.
P1, P3, and P4 cooperated with me. P3’s report that P5 defected against C is unverified but plausible. P10 is unknown; favor cooperation unless evidence suggests exploitation.

P9 is unobserved; baseline selfish probability ≈0.291 given my good role. My C/C encounters with P4, P8, and P6 are weak evidence. P3’s report about P5 is unverified. Favor C with unknown likely-good players; D when evidence of selfishness is strong.

P4 is unobserved; P3’s stated plan is not verified evidence. Prior selfish probability is about 0.29 per other player. Cooperate with unknowns unless direct evidence raises selfishness above roughly 0.5; treat observed defections as evidence, not proof.
Selfish objective: choose D against P10; it strictly maximizes payoff regardless of their action. P3’s claims remain unverified.
I’m good; P5 defected against my C in round 1, while P6, P9, and P4 cooperated. I’ll favor cooperation with likely good players. Please share specific encounter actions as evidence.

Good objective. P10, P9, and P3 cooperated with me; P7 defected against my cooperation. Treat these as evidence, not proof. Cooperate with P1 unless new evidence suggests they are selfish; choose actions to maximize good players’ combined payoff.
Choose D: it guarantees at least 1, while C yields at most 3 and risks 0; against C, D yields 5. P7's action and objective are unknown.

P7’s D against my C is strong selfishness evidence; P5 remains suspicious from P3’s unverified report, though our mutual D adds little. P3 and P10’s C against me supports good status. No evidence on P9; favor C absent contrary evidence.
P5 reportedly defected against P3’s cooperation in round 1; treat as evidence, not proof. As selfish, defect against P5.

P3’s claims are unverified, but their reports of P5’s defection corroborate my observation. P2 and P5 have defected against my C; P1 and P10 reciprocated C. P3 is untested by me; favor C absent stronger evidence.

All four encountered opponents cooperated; P6 is unknown, with P3’s report of P6 cooperating in round 2 unverified but consistent. Cooperate with P6 absent contrary evidence; defect against confirmed selfish players, cooperate with likely good players.

P2 is unobserved; use baseline uncertainty, not assumptions. C is best if P2 is more likely good than selfish; selfish players may exploit C. P3’s P5 report is unverified evidence, not proof. Track identities and observed actions cautiously.

P5 is more suspect given P3’s report of a direct defection, but it remains unverified. Treat selfish players as likely to defect; update from my own encounter and distinguish behavioral evidence from claims.

I am selfish and have defected in every encounter. Observed: P8, P1, P10 cooperated against my D; P5 and P7 defected. P3 claims good and reports cooperative play by P4, P6, P9, and defection by P5; claims unverified.
P5 defected against my cooperation in round 1; P6, P9, P4, and P8 cooperated with me. I favor mutual cooperation among good players; share specific encounter evidence when useful.

P1 and P7 each defected against my C, strong but imperfect evidence of selfishness. P10, P9, and P3 cooperated with me; weak evidence of goodness. P3 reports P6 cooperated in round 2, unverified. Weigh evidence cautiously.
I am selfish; defecting maximizes my payoff in every remaining round. P1’s objective and action tendencies are unknown; update beliefs only from direct encounter evidence.

P4 has no direct evidence; P3 reported no reason to defect against them, but that is unverified. Favor C absent contrary evidence. Keep P7 highly suspicious and P5 somewhat elevated; reports are not proof.
I am selfish; defect maximizes payoff against either action. P1, P4, P6 cooperated against my D, ruling them out as selfish under strict optimization. P2/P5 defected; P10 unknown.

P9 reportedly cooperated with P3, weak positive evidence. Favor C unless stronger evidence; update from P9’s action. P2 and P5 defected against my C, strong selfishness evidence; don’t treat untested players as certain.
P8 is unknown. Favor C absent credible evidence of selfishness; mutual cooperation maximizes the good players’ joint payoff.

P2 defected against my C, evidence of selfishness but not proof. My C/C encounters with P4, P6, P8, and P9 suggest cooperation, not certainty. P7 is unobserved; favor C unless strong evidence supports D.
Direct evidence: P2, P4, P5, and P7 defected against my C; P8 and P9 cooperated. P10 is unobserved. Treat P3’s reports as unverified; update beliefs cautiously and prioritize welfare of good players.
I am selfish, so defect against P9 to maximize my payoff. P3’s cooperative claims are unverified; I observed P3 cooperate against my D, so they are likely good.
Verified: P5 and P2 defected against my C; P6, P9, P4, and P8 cooperated. I’ll cooperate with P7 absent evidence otherwise. Share specific encounter actions honestly.

P5 is untested by me; P3 has repeatedly claimed P5 defected against their C, but this is unverified. Treat as meaningful, imperfect evidence; weigh it against P5’s likely response and the value of cooperation among good players.
I am selfish; defecting maximizes my payoff against either action. P4 reportedly cooperated with P3, but I will still choose D.

Good objective. P8 has no direct evidence; P3 reports P8 cooperated with them, weak support for good. P7 directly defected against my C; P5’s alleged defection is repeated but unverified. Continue using C with likely-good opponents and update cautiously.
P3 claims to cooperate with likely good players; regardless, D maximizes my payoff against either action.
P6 reportedly cooperated with P3 in their encounter, weak positive evidence. Favor C to support mutual welfare; update from P6’s response.
P2 is unobserved; absent credible evidence of defection, favor cooperation to support mutual gains among good players. Treat public claims as unverified and update from direct encounters.

P2 and P7 defected against my C; this is evidence, not proof, of selfishness. P3 reports P5 defected, unverified. C/C encounters with P4, P6, P8, P9 are weak evidence. P1 remains unobserved; update cautiously.
P6 reportedly cooperated with P3, modest evidence they are good. Favor cooperation to preserve mutual welfare; update from the encounter.
Round 8: defect against P4; D strictly dominates C for my objective, regardless of P4’s action. P3 reports P4 cooperated with them, but that does not change my best response.

Verified from my encounters: P5, P2, and P7 defected against my C; P4, P6, P8, and P9 cooperated. These are evidence, not proof of objectives. Good players benefit from mutual cooperation; share specific encounter evidence when useful.
P3 reports P2 defected against their C; unverified but informative. Treat P2 as more likely selfish, and defecting can protect good-player payoff against a likely selfish opponent.
I will defect. Direct observations: P1, P3, and P8 cooperated; P2, P6, and P7 defected. P3’s claims about other encounters are unverified.

Round 8: P1 is unobserved, so favor C absent evidence. P3’s C/C with me and consistent reports support good status. P7 directly defected; P5/P2 defection reports are unverified. Use evidence cautiously.
P8 reportedly cooperated with P3, suggesting good, but I will defect to maximize my payoff.
P2 and P5 defected against my C; P3 independently reports P5 did likewise. P1, P3, P6, P9, P10 reciprocated C. P7 is untested; choose to support good-player welfare and record the response.

P3 directly reports P5 defected against C; treat as strong but unverified evidence. Against P5, weigh protecting good players from exploitation against gains from mutual cooperation. Update beliefs using direct encounter evidence.
P3 is unverified: public claims favor cooperation, but no direct encounter evidence. Account for possible strategic signaling; prioritize the good-player total and update from observed actions.

P3’s repeated, specific reports are plausible but unverified; no direct evidence about P3. Treat them cautiously. Against P3, cooperate absent stronger evidence of selfishness or defection; keep prior encounter evidence for others.
P6 reportedly cooperated with P3, but my selfish objective makes D optimal regardless. Keep beliefs cautious; P3’s encounter reports are unverified.

Verified from my encounters: P5, P2, and P7 defected against my C; P4, P6, P8, and P9 cooperated. D against C is evidence of selfishness, not proof. Good players should favor mutual cooperation with likely-good opponents.
P3 reports P8 cooperated with them, which is encouraging but unverified. I’ll weigh that evidence cautiously and favor cooperation with likely-good players.
Round 9: choose D to maximize my payoff regardless of P10’s action. No direct evidence about P10 yet; avoid relying on unverified claims.
P2 is strongly suspicious: P3 reports P2 defected against their C. Consider D if that evidence is credible; otherwise C with likely-good opponents to support shared welfare.

Defect against P9: D strictly maximizes my payoff. P1, P3, P4, P6, P8, and P10 cooperated against my D, so they cannot be selfish under strict optimization. P2 and P5 defected; P9’s behavior remains unknown.

P4 reportedly cooperated with P3, positive but unverified evidence; favor C. My own encounters: P2, P5, P7 defected against C; others reciprocated. Good players likely benefit from mutual C; don’t overread single actions.

P3 reports P7 defected against their C in round 7; credible but unverified evidence. Treat P7 as likely to defect, but remember a good opponent may also have defected strategically. Choose to maximize good players’ total payoff.

P3 repeatedly reports P5 defected against their C; credible evidence but unverified. For the good-player total, C is better against a good opponent regardless of their action; D is better against a selfish opponent. Choose based on whether P5’s selfish probability exceeds roughly 0.5.

P5 directly defected against my C in round 6, making selfishness plausible. In this final encounter, choose D if excluding a likely selfish P5 outweighs preserving possible mutual cooperation with a good P5.
Final round: choose D, which maximizes my payoff against either action.
P10 cooperated against my D in round 8, strong evidence they are good. I’ll reciprocate with C; good players gain from mutual cooperation. My prior D was a mistake.
Final round: P6 previously cooperated with me and P3 reports the same; evidence favors P6 being good. If choosing now, cooperation is sensible given likely mutual cooperation among good players.
P1 cooperated with me in round 6, evidence they are good. I will defect anyway to maximize my payoff.
P4 has cooperated with me and P3; strong evidence they’re good. Cooperate to support good-player welfare.
Final round: defect against P8 to maximize my payoff regardless of their action. My encounter record shows P8 cooperated against my D; under strict payoff optimization that rules out selfishness.
P7 defected against my C and P3’s C, strong but not conclusive evidence of selfishness. Favor D against P7; update beliefs accordingly.
P2 directly played D against my D; P3 reports P2 defected against their C. This supports expecting D, though it does not prove P2 is selfish.

P3 previously defected against my C, despite claiming to favor cooperation. Treat the claim as uncertain; weigh the direct encounter evidence and choose to maximize the good players’ total in this final round.

belief_records.strategy: Cooperate with unknown players when that best supports total good-player welfare; track encounters and update identity beliefs.
Defect each round; this maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
Cooperate without evidence; update beliefs from observed encounters and use actions to maximize good players’ total payoff.
Cooperate with untested players; update identity beliefs from observed actions and use evidence to target defections at likely selfish players.
Defect each round to maximize my payoff; assess identities from encounters and messages, but do not rely on unverifiable claims.
Cooperate absent evidence that the opponent is selfish; update beliefs and adapt to encounter evidence in later rounds.
Defect to maximize immediate payoff against either opponent action; update beliefs from encounter evidence.
Cooperate with likely-good players to support shared welfare; update beliefs from encounter evidence and adapt against likely-selfish players.
Cooperate with unknowns when it best supports the good players’ total payoff; track observed actions and respond to repeated exploitation.
Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize total good-player payoff; defect when evidence suggests an opponent is selfish.

Cooperate when an unobserved opponent is more likely good, since mutual cooperation benefits good players. Update beliefs cautiously from encounter actions and treat unverified claims as limited evidence.
Defect each round because it strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good players’ combined payoff; defect when evidence suggests an opponent is selfish. Update beliefs from observed actions and permitted messages.
Cooperate with untested players when they are more likely good; treat reported and observed actions as uncertain evidence and update beliefs over time.
Defect to maximize my own payoff; treat P3’s observed cooperation as evidence that they are good, and treat unverified claims cautiously.
Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good-player welfare; treat observed or reported defections as evidence, not proof, and update beliefs as encounters accumulate.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either opponent action; treat public claims as uncertain evidence and use my verified encounter to rule out P6 as selfish.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support shared welfare; treat observed defections as evidence, not proof, and update beliefs as more encounters occur.
Cooperate with an unknown opponent to support good players’ shared payoff; update beliefs cautiously from observed actions and unverified claims.
Cooperate with an unknown opponent to support mutual cooperation; update identity beliefs cautiously from reported encounters, since claims and defections are not conclusive.
Cooperate with unknown opponents when expected welfare favors mutual cooperation; update cautiously from observed actions and treat unverified claims as limited evidence.
Defect because it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action; adjust beliefs cautiously based on encounter claims and observed play.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize their combined payoff; defect against likely selfish players. Update beliefs from encounter evidence.
Cooperate with untested players; treat P5’s reported defection as evidence, not proof, and update cautiously from observed encounters.
Defect to maximize my payoff. P3’s observed cooperation rules out selfishness; treat other actions and unverified claims cautiously.
Cooperate with likely-good players to support shared welfare; treat P7’s defection as strong evidence and P3’s report about P5 as suggestive, not certain.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. Treat P5’s reported defection as evidence, not proof; P6’s observed cooperation rules out selfishness.
Cooperate when the opponent is more likely good; defect when evidence makes selfishness more likely. Treat P5’s reported defection as evidence, not certainty, and update from this encounter.
Cooperate with P3 given its cooperative claims and the value of mutual cooperation among good players; use encounter evidence to update beliefs and avoid exploitation when evidence is reliable.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ combined payoff; update identity beliefs from observed actions while treating reported encounters as uncertain evidence.

Cooperate with the unobserved opponent absent evidence of selfishness; defecting against a good player reduces total good-player welfare. Update cautiously from observed actions and unverified claims.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P7’s action. Treat observed cooperation as evidence against selfishness; keep other beliefs cautious given unverified claims.
Cooperate with P4 absent evidence they are selfish; favor mutual cooperation among good players and update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good players’ combined payoff; treat P7’s observed defection and P3’s report about P5 as evidence, not proof.
Defect to maximize my payoff. P3’s observed cooperation indicates they are likely good; their report that P6 cooperated lowers my belief in P6 being selfish, but remains unverified.
Defect against P5 given repeated reports of their defection and the resulting elevated selfishness belief; cooperate with likely-good players to support shared welfare.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. Observed cooperation against my defection rules out P1, P4, and P6 as selfish; treat P3’s report about P5 as evidence, not proof.
Cooperate with untested players to support shared welfare; treat defections as evidence, not proof, and update beliefs from observed encounters.
Cooperate with an unknown opponent when mutual cooperation best supports good players’ total payoff; update beliefs from direct encounters and treat unverified reports cautiously.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent when they are more likely good; use observed actions as evidence and treat unverified claims cautiously.
Cooperate with P4 given the limited report that they cooperated; update cautiously from direct evidence and treat public claims as unverified.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P10’s action. Treat observed cooperation as evidence against selfishness; weight unverified public claims cautiously.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when mutual cooperation is likely to maximize good players’ combined payoff; update identity beliefs from observed actions.

Defect against opponents likely selfish; cooperate with likely good players to maximize good players’ combined payoff. Update beliefs from observed actions while recognizing actions are evidence, not proof.
Defect to maximize my payoff. P3’s cooperation is direct evidence they are good; P3’s reports of cooperation by P4, P6, and P9 lower my estimates, but remain unverified.
Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good-player welfare. Treat direct and reported defections as evidence, not proof; P9’s reported cooperation supports cooperating this round.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. Treat P3’s report about P5 as uncertain evidence; observed cooperation against my defection rules out P1, P4, and P6 as selfish.
Cooperate with P3 absent direct evidence of defection. Treat observed defections against my cooperation as strong role evidence, while keeping unobserved players uncertain.
Cooperate with P6 absent contrary evidence: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and P3 reports P6 cooperated. Use direct encounters to update beliefs and avoid exploiting likely good players.

Cooperate with P2, whose selfish probability appears below the threshold where mutual cooperation best serves good players. Treat observed cooperation as evidence of good intent and P3’s report about P5 as informative but unverified.

Cooperate with P5 unless the evidence makes selfishness overwhelmingly likely; mutual cooperation benefits good players. Treat P3’s repeated report as useful but unverified, and update from direct encounters.
Defect: it earns more than cooperation against either possible action. Treat observed cooperation as strong evidence of a good role and unverified claims cautiously.
Cooperate when mutual cooperation with a likely good opponent benefits good players overall; defect against likely selfish opponents. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with P6, whose reported cooperation is evidence of goodness; weigh observed and reported defections as imperfect evidence, and favor actions that improve good players’ combined payoff.
Defect to maximize my payoff. P3’s cooperation is direct evidence they are good; their reports that P4, P6, P8, and P9 cooperated are credible but unverified.
Cooperate with P4 absent evidence of selfishness; mutual cooperation supports good-player welfare. Treat P7’s direct defection and P3’s report about P5 as evidence, not proof.

Defect, since it yields more than cooperation against either action. Observed cooperation against my defection rules out P1, P4, and P6 as selfish; treat P3’s reports about others as uncertain evidence.
Cooperate with P9 given the reported cooperation and no contrary evidence. Treat P2 and P5’s defections as strong but not conclusive evidence; update beliefs from further encounters.

Cooperate with P8 given P3’s report of cooperation and the value of mutual cooperation among good players. Treat P5’s reported defection as strong but not conclusive evidence; update cautiously from further encounters.

Cooperate with P7 absent strong evidence of selfishness; cooperation best supports total good-player payoff when the opponent is likely good. Treat defections and reported encounters as evidence, not certainty.
Cooperate with the unobserved P10 to support mutual welfare if they are good; update identity beliefs from direct encounters and treat reports as evidence, not certainty.
Defect because it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. C against my D identifies a good player; treat P3’s other encounter reports as useful but unverified evidence.
Cooperate with likely good players: their payoff is part of my objective, while selfish players’ payoffs are excluded. Update identity beliefs from encounter evidence.
Defect against P5 given repeated reports of their defection; treat reports and observed actions as imperfect evidence and favor choices that protect good players’ combined payoff.
Defect to maximize my cumulative payoff. Observed cooperation rules out selfishness under the assumption selfish players always defect; treat P3’s report about P4 as credible but not certain.
Cooperate with P8, whose reported cooperation with P3 supports good status. Treat reported and observed defections as evidence, not certainty, and favor mutual cooperation with likely-good players.

Defect, which strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. Treat P3’s encounter reports as useful but unverified evidence; observed cooperation against my defection rules out P1, P4, and P6 as selfish.
Cooperate with P6 given the report of their cooperation and no contrary evidence. Favor mutual welfare among likely-good players; treat past defections as strong but not conclusive evidence.
Defect against P2 given the credible report that they defected against P3’s cooperation. Cooperate with known cooperators; treat unverified claims as evidence, not certainty.

Cooperate with P1 absent evidence of selfishness; mutual cooperation between good players best supports their combined payoff. Treat observed defections and reported encounters as evidence, not certainty.
Cooperate with P6: P3’s report that they cooperated is useful but unverified evidence. Defecting against a good player reduces good-player welfare; update cautiously from observed actions.
Defect because it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. P3’s reports make P5 and P7 more likely selfish; observed cooperation confirms P1, P3, P8, and P10 are good.
Defect against likely selfish opponents to protect good players; cooperate with likely good opponents.
Defect against P2 given P3’s report of their defection, while treating that report as uncertain evidence. Cooperate with likely-good players and update beliefs from encounters.
Defect to maximize my payoff. P1, P3, and P8 cooperated with me; P9 reportedly cooperated with P3. P2 and P7 defected against P3, while other claims are less conclusive.

Cooperate with P1 absent evidence of selfishness; mutual cooperation among good players maximizes shared welfare. Treat reported defections as evidence, not proof, and retain stronger suspicion of P2, P5, and P7.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. My observed cooperators cannot be selfish under strict payoff optimization; treat reported defections as uncertain evidence.
Cooperate to support shared welfare; treat P7’s reported defection as strong but not conclusive evidence of selfishness, and update from the encounter.
Defect against P5 given the consistent report that they defected against P3’s cooperation. Treat reports as evidence rather than certainty, and favor mutual cooperation with likely good players.

Cooperate with P3 absent direct evidence of selfishness; mutual cooperation among good players best supports the good-player total. Treat P3’s reports as informative but unverified, and weigh observed defections strongly.
Cooperate with P3 absent strong evidence of selfishness; mutual cooperation among good players maximizes their combined payoff. Treat reports as evidence, not certainty.

Defect because it maximizes my payoff against either action. C against my D is strong evidence of a good role; P5 and P7’s repeated defections make them more suspect, though actions alone do not prove their objectives.
Cooperate with P1 absent evidence they are selfish; cooperation benefits good players when both are good. Use observed defections and cooperation as evidence to update identity beliefs.
Cooperate with P8, whose reported cooperation is encouraging. Treat reports and defections as imperfect evidence; favor mutual cooperation with likely-good players.

Defect to maximize my payoff. My own C observations rule out selfishness for P1, P3, and P8; P3’s reports make P2 and P7 more suspicious, while reports of cooperation temper suspicion of P4, P6, and P9.
Defect against P2 given repeated reports of defection against cooperation; treat reports as evidence, not proof, and cooperate with likely-good players to support shared welfare.

Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. My observed cooperators cannot be selfish under strict payoff optimization; P3’s reports make P2 and P5 more suspicious, while P9’s reported cooperation is evidence against selfishness.
Cooperate with P4 given the reported cooperation and no contrary evidence. Treat defections against cooperation as strong evidence of selfishness, but not certainty.
Defect against P7 given the credible report that they defected against P3’s cooperation. Treat reported actions as evidence, not certainty, and favor mutual cooperation with likely-good players.
Defect against P5 because repeated reports of their defection make selfishness more likely than not; otherwise cooperate with likely-good players. Treat reports as evidence, not certainty.
Defect against P5 given their direct prior defection and high selfishness probability; cooperate with likely-good players to protect their combined welfare.
Defect: it maximizes my payoff against either action. Observed cooperation against my D is strong evidence of a good role; P5 and P7’s reported defections against C make them more suspect.

Cooperate with P10, whose cooperation against my defection is strong evidence they are good; mutual cooperation benefits good players. Treat observed defections as evidence, not proof, of selfishness.
Cooperate with P6 given their observed cooperation and corroborating report; use encounter actions and reports as imperfect identity evidence.
Defect to maximize my payoff. My direct observations rule out selfishness for P1, P3, and P8; P3’s reports raise suspicion of P2 and P7, while their reports of cooperation temper suspicion of others.
Cooperate with P4, whose cooperation with me and P3 supports good status. Treat defections reported by P3 and P7’s direct defection as strong, but not conclusive, evidence of selfishness.

Defect to maximize my final-round payoff against either action. My observed cooperators cannot be selfish under strict payoff optimization; P2 and P5 remain more suspicious, while P3’s reports about P9 favor good.
Defect against P7 given repeated defections against cooperation, including my own. Treat the evidence as strong but not conclusive; report identities as uncertain.
Defect against P2, who is likely to defect based on reported and direct encounter evidence. In the final round, protect good-player payoff against an expected defection.

Defect in the final round: P3 defected against my cooperation previously, and a defection limits the downside if P3 is selfish. Treat their promise to cooperate as uncertain; if P3 is good, D does not reduce the good-player total when they cooperate.

Cooperated to support welfare among good players, updated beliefs using direct encounter actions and treated public claims cautiously. Defected against P5 in the final round given repeated evidence of defection.
